frontier.hypothesis: The residual is a sched2 register-REUSE fact: target's window keeps only two call-clobbered temps live because $v0 carries idx1's address chain and is then reused for arg3's chain, and that anti-dependence is the extra edge that lets arg4's address chain be stretched across the window.
frontier.mechanism: The s40 rank-order derivation shows target's order requires an edge sched1's true-dependence graph does not contain; the only edges available at sched2 are hard-register anti-dependences, and target's $v0 reuse is exactly one. f17 is the only family with target's $a0 map but it keeps $a0, $v1 and $v0 live at once, so no reuse occurs.
frontier.next_probe: On the f17 family (arg4 and arg3 as value locals; drop the inert index local), sweep spellings that force arg5's VALUE load to be emitted before arg3's index load - arg5 hoisted as a value local placed before arg3's, arg5 hoisted while arg3 is left inline, arg5's value passed through a local - and for each read the .greg/.sched2 dump for how many call-clobbered temps are live across the window and whether any $v0 anti-dependence links the arg5 and arg3 chains. Score live anything that drops the live temp count to two.

frontier.hypothesis: Priority, not LUID, decides the leaf-load picks, so the lever is the LENGTH of one argument's dependence chain - a genuinely different expression for one argument, not a different spelling of the same one.
frontier.mechanism: s34 found nearly every window insn carries LAUNCH_PRIORITY so the priority term looked like a constant tie, and s40 proved the LUID term is inert for the leaves. If both were truly inert the emission could not vary at all, yet 11 distinct functions exist - so one of the two is live in a way the ledger has not measured. INSN_PRIORITY is the longest path to the block end, so an argument whose chain is one insn longer changes every rank in the window.
frontier.next_probe: Dump BB2_PRIO_DEBUG for three forms with different windows (c_0000_435, c_0010_435, c_0110_435) and tabulate the actual INSN_PRIORITY of all 15 window insns in each. If priorities differ across forms, s34's 'constant tie' is scoped too broadly and the priority column is the live lever; then compute from the s40 rank-constraint table which priority assignment produces target's order and which chain-length change realises it.

frontier.hypothesis: The window's emission is invariant under sixteen distinct named-local spellings, so the only remaining source-side variable is the surrounding chassis's register pressure - how many callee-saved bases are live across the timeout block - not the block's own spelling.
frontier.mechanism: All four live families differ only in whether arg3 and arg4 are value locals. Target's window needs $v0 reused across two chains, which happens only when the allocator is short of call-clobbered temps. The chassis hoists THREE table pointers into callee-saved registers before the loop; the s9 H37/H38 allocation argument fixes the callee-saved MAP but says nothing about the window's temp count, so this quadrant is genuinely open.
frontier.next_probe: Cross the two axes for the first time: {0,1,2,3 hoisted table pointer locals, the rest read directly as globals inside the block} x {arg3 value local on/off} x {arg4 value local on/off}, about 16 forms. For each record the number of distinct call-clobbered registers live inside the printf window and whether $v0 is reused across two chains; score live anything reaching two.
